title: GOLDMEMBER — CD169/CD196 identity reconciliation
scope: Resolve the cruise identifier conflict before any offline-tape TOBI bytes are admitted, and freeze a synthetic-vs-real comparison contract before primary data arrival.

public_evidence.finding: RRS Charles Darwin Cruise 169 ran 17 Feb-19 Mar 2005 and explicitly used TOBI deep-tow sidescan on the southern Mid-Atlantic Ridge. JD059 is within the cruise narrative and TOBI operations.
CD180 (20 May-9 Jun 2006) is documented as the last scientific cruise for NERC of RRS Charles Darwin.
RRS James Cook replaced the ageing RRS Charles Darwin after its 2006 retirement.

hard_boundary: Do not tell the custodian their identifier is wrong as a settled fact. Ask for confirmation because the public record strongly indicates CD169 while the reply says CD196.

comparison_order: receive and hash original bytes/file manifest
extract only the frozen 01:00-01:29 UTC window
run the already-frozen synthetic expectation and same metrics
preserve a null or contradiction as a valid negative result
forbidden: tuning synthetic parameters after seeing real sonar
moving the target window after inspection
promoting a historical/archaeological identity from morphology alone

claim_ceiling: Public evidence strongly supports CD169 as the requested cruise and makes CD196 implausible as an RRS Charles Darwin cruise number; final reconciliation remains with BODC/NOC custodian confirmation.
